comparator.name: Muziekwetenschap
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026-27 programme-specific EER defines a 120-EC Musicology major and 60 EC of profiling space. The major consists of eight compulsory 7.5-EC foundation courses (60 EC), Philosophy of Science (7.5 EC), the Musicology Research Seminar (7.5 EC), the BA Musicology Thesis (7.5 EC), one compulsory 30-EC depth package and one 7.5-EC restricted choice. The first-listed depth package, Music and Society, and the first-listed restricted choice, Art, Culture and Society, are selected as neutral official-order tie-breaks without reference to UCR fit. Within the 60-EC profiling space, at least 30 EC must form an approved profile package; the profile package and remaining 30 EC of genuine free-choice space are preserved without inventing subjects. The resulting pathway accounts for exactly 180 EC.

routeSelection.basis: The generic Musicology target requires one of two 30-EC depth packages and one of two 7.5-EC context courses to instantiate the full major. Music and Society and Art, Culture and Society are each listed first in the adopted 2026-27 EER, so they are selected as neutral official-order tie-breaks. The 60-EC profiling space remains generic because the regulations deliberately leave its approved subject matter to the student. These judgments were fixed before UCR course fit was considered.

exception.reason: Utrecht's 180-EC Musicology pathway is defined by a compulsory sequence in notation and aural skills, harmony and form, music history before 1600, music from 1600 to 1900 and music from 1900 to the present, popular-music analysis and critical listening, music in screen media, advanced music analysis and criticism, music-theatre study and dedicated musicological research culminating in a Musicology thesis. UCR offers no course in music, music theory, aural skills, music history, music analysis or musicology. Its film, media, communication, literature, art, history and cultural-analysis courses can illuminate isolated social or media contexts around music, but they cannot make 23 non-PPD courses contribute concretely to a Musicology concept or reproduce the programme's defining disciplinary sequence. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be a media-and-culture degree with occasional musical examples, not a defensible Musicology curriculum.
exception.curriculumContext: The adopted 2026-27 curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: a 120-EC major and 60 EC of profiling space. The major contains 60 EC of compulsory first-year foundations, a 7.5-EC academic-context course, a 7.5-EC research seminar, a 7.5-EC bachelor thesis, one 30-EC advanced depth package and one 7.5-EC restricted choice. The selected first-listed Music and Society package comprises Music and Theatre, Music Analysis and Criticism, Music and Nature, and Dutch Music Cultures. The profiling space preserves an approved 30-EC profile package and 30 EC of genuine free choice without inventing subjects.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. The workbook contains no course whose disciplinary object is music or musicology and no course in notation, harmony, aural training, music history, music analysis, performance studies or musicological methods. MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media and MCCLITR311 Film & Text address film form and include sound among audiovisual elements; MCCMEDI212 Media & the Environment includes sound and digital media; MCCCOMM312 Creative Communication Laboratory treats rhythm and sound as poetic or conceptual material while expressly excluding music performance; MCCMEDI311 Media & Race, GOSHIST311 Native American Histories and several other cultural courses include music only as one example among broader media or artistic expressions. MCCMEDI312 The Documentary can include audio production. These are adjacent media, communication, literature and history offerings, not a musicological curriculum. They cannot supply a progressive theory-and-aural-skills sequence, sustained music history, advanced music analysis or a dedicated Musicology research trajectory, so constructing a 24-course comparison would misrepresent UCR's teaching.
